answer_text:
Let

\[
I(f)=\int_0^1 (f''(x))^2\,dx.
\]

Since \(f\in C^2[0,1]\), Taylor’s formula with integral remainder gives

\[
f(1)=f(0)+f'(0)+\int_0^1 (1-x)f''(x)\,dx.
\]

Using the boundary conditions \(f(0)=f(1)=0\) and \(f'(0)=2\), we get

\[
0=0+2+\int_0^1 (1-x)f''(x)\,dx,
\]

so

\[
\int_0^1 (1-x)f''(x)\,dx=-2.
\]

Now apply Cauchy–Schwarz:

\[
4=\left|\int_0^1 (1-x)f''(x)\,dx\right|^2
\le \left(\int_0^1 (1-x)^2\,dx\right)\left(\int_0^1 (f''(x))^2\,dx\right).
\]

Compute

\[
\int_0^1 (1-x)^2\,dx=\frac13.
\]

Therefore,

\[
4\le \frac13 I(f),
\]

which implies

\[
I(f)\ge 12.
\]

Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz occurs when \(f''(x)\) is proportional to \(1-x\). Since

\[
\int_0^1 (1-x)f''(x)\,dx=-2,
\]

we take

\[
f''(x)=-6(1-x)=6x-6.
\]

Integrating and using \(f(0)=0\), \(f'(0)=2\),

\[
f'(x)=3x^2-6x+2,
\]

\[
f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2x.
\]

This function satisfies all the conditions, and

\[
\int_0^1 (f''(x))^2\,dx
=
\int_0^1 (6x-6)^2\,dx
=
36\int_0^1 (x-1)^2\,dx
=
36\cdot \frac13
=
12.
\]

Thus the minimum value is

\[
\boxed{12}.
\]
